sourceBlog.title: Korea Arrival Checklist for Travelers & Digital Nomads (2026)

introSlide.heading: Landing in Korea for the first time?
introSlide.description: Here's what to do in order.

slides.heading: 1. Get local apps: they just work better
slides.description: Naver Map + Papago. Locals use these. English supported.

slides.heading: 2. Foreign cards don't always work
slides.description: Small shops accept Korean cards only. Bring some cash or get a WOWPASS.

slides.heading: 3. Grab a WOWPASS at Incheon Airport
slides.description: Prepaid payment + transit card in one. Load with your native card.

slides.heading: 4. AREX train to Seoul: fastest way in
slides.description: Express ₩11,000 (43 min). All-Stop ₩4,750 (60 min). Tap your WOWPASS.

slides.heading: 5. Uber works for taxis
slides.description: Want more options? Get KakaoTaxi. It's what locals use.

slides.heading: 6. Staying long-term? ARC, then phone, then bank
slides.description: This sequence unlocks Korean payments, delivery apps, and more.

caption:
Your foreign Visa card might get you through the airport, but that kimbap place around the corner? Cash only.

Korea runs on local payment systems like Samsung Pay and Kakao Pay. Your foreign card works at big chains and hotels, but smaller spots often don't accept it. The easy fix: get a WOWPASS card at Incheon (works almost everywhere) and keep some cash on hand.

For getting around, Naver Map beats Google Maps here. It's what locals use, and it supports English. Same with Papago for translation.

Planning to stay longer? There's a setup sequence: ARC, then phone plan, then bank account. Each step unlocks the next. But if you're just visiting, WOWPASS + cash + local apps will cover you.
